questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meristematic and Permanent Tissues' refers to.
questions.a: Plant tissues are grouped into meristematic tissues of actively dividing cells at apical, intercalary and lateral positions, and permanent tissues, which are simple tissues like parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma, and complex tissues like xylem and phloem.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meristematic and Permanent Tissues'.
questions.a: Xylem conducts water with tracheids, vessels, fibres and parenchyma, while phloem translocates food through sieve tubes, companion cells and phloem fibres.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meristematic and Permanent Tissues' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Monocot and Dicot Root, Stem and Leaf Anatomy

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Monocot and Dicot Root, Stem and Leaf Anatomy' refers to.
questions.a: Internal anatomy distinguishes dicot and monocot organs: dicot roots show xylem and phloem in separate radial bundles with exarch xylem, monocot stems have scattered vascular bundles with no cambium, and dicot leaves show reticulate venation with mesophyll split into palisade and spongy parenchyma.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Monocot and Dicot Root, Stem and Leaf Anatomy'.
questions.a: Ground tissue system, vascular tissue system and epidermal tissue system together build the internal structure of root, stem and leaf in both groups.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Monocot and Dicot Root, Stem and Leaf Anatomy' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Secondary Growth: Cambium, Annual Rings, Heartwood and Sapwood

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Secondary Growth: Cambium, Annual Rings, Heartwood and Sapwood' refers to.
questions.a: In dicot stems and roots secondary growth arises from the vascular cambium and cork cambium, which form secondary xylem, secondary phloem, and periderm; activity differences form spring wood and autumn wood or annual rings, and the darker inner wood becomes heartwood while the outer functional wood is sapwood.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Secondary Growth: Cambium, Annual Rings, Heartwood and Sapwood'.
questions.a: Cork cambium produces phellem and phelloderm making up periderm, which replaces the epidermis of the older stem and protects it.
